_comment: Master spec, part 1 of 2: sciences. Each field: source (authoritative published standard) + units in teaching order. The expander turns this into syllabus/*.json + planned rows. Lesson levels: f=foundational, i=intermediate, a=advanced, e=expert.

biochemistry.note: Units follow the course's canonical arc — structure and function of the major molecule classes, then enzyme mechanism and regulation, then central metabolism — the sequence every biochemistry course teaches.

units.title: Protein structure and function
topics: Amino acids and the peptide bond

lesson.title: Protein Structure and Function
lesson.summary: From twenty amino acids to folded machines — how sequence determines structure and structure determines function.

lesson.title: Enzyme Kinetics and Mechanism
lesson.summary: How enzymes lower activation barriers — catalytic strategies, the Michaelis-Menten model and the meaning of Km and Vmax.

lesson.title: Hemoglobin and Allostery
lesson.summary: The classic allosteric machine — cooperative oxygen binding, the Bohr effect and what sickle-cell disease reveals.

lesson.title: Glycolysis and Sugar Chemistry
lesson.summary: How glucose is split for energy — the ten steps of glycolysis, their logic and their regulation.

units.title: The citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation
topics: Pyruvate oxidation and the TCA cycle

lesson.title: Respiration: TCA Cycle and Oxidative Phosphorylation
lesson.summary: Where most ATP is made — pyruvate oxidation, the citric acid cycle and the proton-motive force driving ATP synthase.

lesson.title: Lipids, Membranes and Transport
lesson.summary: The bilayer as a selective barrier — lipid chemistry, fluidity and the proteins that move things across.

units.title: DNA, RNA and the flow of information

lesson.title: Nucleic Acids and Information Flow
lesson.summary: Replication, transcription and translation as chemistry — the central dogma at molecular resolution.

lesson.title: Metabolic Integration and Regulation
lesson.summary: How the body switches between fuels — insulin, glucagon and the logic of the fed and fasting states.

lesson.title: Biochemical Methods and Frontiers
lesson.summary: How biochemistry is actually measured — chromatography, electrophoresis, mass spectrometry and structural biology.

source.track: university · introductory for majors, open curriculum

microbiology.note: Units follow the textbook's own chapter arc: microbial cell biology and genetics, then systematics across the microbial world, then disease, immunity and applied microbiology.

lesson.title: The Microbial World
lesson.summary: How we discovered the invisible world and learned to name, classify and see it.

lesson.title: Prokaryotic Cell Structure
lesson.summary: Inside a bacterial cell — walls, membranes, flagella, plasmids and the architecture of biofilms.

lesson.title: Microbial Metabolism and Growth
lesson.summary: How microbes eat and multiply — metabolic diversity, fermentation and the mathematics of growth curves.

lesson.title: Microbial Genetics
lesson.summary: Why bacterial evolution is so fast — mutation, transformation, transduction and conjugation.

lesson.title: Viruses and Bacteriophages
lesson.summary: The simplest replicators — lytic and lysogenic cycles, phage therapy and the strange world of prions.

lesson.title: Microbial Diversity and Systematics
lesson.summary: A tour of the tree's deep branches — archaea, Gram stains as deep splits, and the eukaryotic microbes.

units.title: Infection, epidemiology and pathogenesis
topics: Portals of entry and virulence factors

lesson.title: Pathogenesis and Epidemiology
lesson.summary: How pathogens enter, adhere, invade and spread — virulence factors and the epidemiologist's toolkit.

lesson.title: Antimicrobials and Resistance
lesson.summary: The arms race — antibiotic classes and targets, and the mechanisms microbes use to evade them.

lesson.title: Applied and Environmental Microbiology
lesson.summary: Microbes at work — water treatment, fermentation industries and the microbiome's role in health.

source.qualification: Integrated Principles of Zoology (Hickman, Roberts, Keen, Larson, I'Anson)
source.document: Canonical zoology textbook, edition 19 chapter structure
source.track: university · majors' introduction to animal biology

zoology.note: Units follow the canonical arc: the animal condition and its origins, then the phyla in phylogenetic order from Porifera to Chordata, closing with ecology and conservation.

units.title: The animal condition and its origins

lesson.title: The Animal Condition
lesson.summary: What defines an animal — body plans, symmetry, tissue layers and the origin of multicellularity.

lesson.title: Sponges, Jellyfish and the First Bodies
lesson.summary: The simplest animals — filter-feeding poriferans and the cnidarians that invented stinging cells and nerves.

units.title: The protostomes I: flatworms to annelids

lesson.title: Worms and Molluscs: the Protostome Radiations
lesson.summary: Bilateral bodies, coeloms and the great protostome radiations — flatworms to segmented worms and molluscs.

lesson.title: Arthropods: the Jointed-Leg Success Story
lesson.summary: Segmentation plus exoskeleton plus joints — how arthropods, above all insects, took over the planet.

lesson.title: Echinoderms and the Chordate Line
lesson.summary: Starfish as our cousins — deuterostomy, the chordate body plan and where backbones came from.

lesson.title: Fishes and the Move onto Land
lesson.summary: Half of all vertebrates are fish — jaws, fins and the lineage that crawled ashore.

lesson.title: Amniotes: Reptiles, Birds and Mammals
lesson.summary: The egg that conquered land — amniote radiations, warm blood and the mammalian body plan.

units.title: Animal physiology: form meets environment
topics: Nervous and sensory systems across phyla

lesson.title: Comparative Physiology
lesson.summary: The same problems, many solutions — how different phyla regulate heat, water and nerves.

lesson.title: Behaviour, Biogeography and Conservation
lesson.summary: Why animals do what they do, where they live and what happens when habitats shrink.

source.qualification: Raven, Evert & Eichhorn — Biology of Plants

botany.note: Units follow the canonical arc: the plant cell and plant life through time, then form and function from cells to ecosystems, closing with ethnobotany and economic plants.

lesson.title: Botany: an Introduction
lesson.summary: Why plants run the planet and how botany studies them — scope, history and methods.

lesson.title: The Plant Cell
lesson.summary: What makes a plant cell a plant cell — walls, chloroplasts, vacuoles and the meristems that keep growing.

units.title: Plant tissues and the vegetative body

lesson.title: Plant Tissues and Organs
lesson.summary: Root to leaf — the tissue systems, and how roots, stems and leaves are built.

units.title: Photosynthesis and plant metabolism
topics: Carbon fixation and the Calvin cycle

lesson.title: Photosynthesis and Plant Metabolism
lesson.summary: The biochemistry that feeds the world — light capture, carbon fixation and drought-proofing alternatives.

lesson.title: Water Relations and Transport
lesson.summary: How water climbs a tree — water potential, the cohesion-tension theory and phloem flow.

lesson.title: Plant Reproduction Through Time
lesson.summary: The life-cycle innovation ladder — spores, seeds and the flower's co-evolution with pollinators.

lesson.title: Plant Genetics and Breeding
lesson.summary: From Mendel's peas to polyploid wheat — plant genetics and the breeding of our crops.

lesson.title: Plant Ecology and Biomes
lesson.summary: Which plants live where, and why — biomes, succession and what happens when species move.

lesson.title: Economic and Ethnobotany
lesson.summary: Plants as food, medicine and material — where crops came from and why plant diversity matters.

source.qualification: Cambridge International AS & A Level Marine Science 9693

marine-science.note: Units follow the syllabus's subject content: ocean basics, then physics and chemistry of seawater, then marine ecosystems and their physiology, closing with energy, fisheries and aquaculture.

lesson.title: Earth, Oceans and Tides
lesson.summary: How ocean basins formed, why tides rise, and how marine scientists partition the sea.

units.title: Seawater: chemistry and physics
topics: Light and sound in the sea

lesson.title: The Physics and Chemistry of Seawater
lesson.summary: What's in seawater and how it moves — salinity, density layers, and how light and sound travel.

lesson.title: Currents, Gyres and Thermohaline Circulation
lesson.summary: The ocean's conveyor belts — wind-driven gyres, the global overturning circulation and El Niño.

units.title: Marine ecosystems: the shelf and the deep
topics: Open ocean and the deep sea

lesson.title: Marine Ecosystems from Shore to Trench
lesson.summary: Ecosystems across the depth zones — reefs, open water, and the chemosynthetic deep.

lesson.title: Plankton and Primary Production
lesson.summary: The ocean's grass is drifting plankton — nutrients, blooms and the marine food web's base.

lesson.title: How Marine Life Works
lesson.summary: Living in salt water — osmoregulation, buoyancy, and adaptations to depth and cold.

lesson.title: Threats to Marine Biodiversity
lesson.summary: What's endangering the sea — bleaching, overfishing, plastics and the pathways of damage.

lesson.title: Fisheries, Mariculture and Sustainable Yield
lesson.summary: Harvesting the sea without emptying it — stock assessment, management and farming the water.

lesson.title: The Ocean and Climate
lesson.summary: The sea as climate regulator — the carbon pump, acidification and the politics of protection.

source.qualification: JetStream — An Online School for Weather

meteorology.note: Units follow JetStream's arc — the atmosphere's makeup and energy, moisture and clouds, then the dynamics of pressure and wind, storms, and the science of forecasting.

lesson.title: The Atmosphere and Its Energy
lesson.summary: The air around us — layers, pressure, and how the sun's energy moves through the system.

lesson.title: Moisture, Clouds and Precipitation
lesson.summary: From vapour to rain — humidity, the ten cloud genera and how droplets grow.

units.title: Pressure, wind and global circulation
topics: The general circulation and jet streams

lesson.title: Wind and the Global Circulation
lesson.summary: Why wind blows and where it goes — gradients, Coriolis, and the planet-scale circulation cells.

units.title: Air masses, fronts and mid-latitude cyclones
topics: The life cycle of a mid-latitude cyclone

lesson.title: Fronts and Mid-Latitude Cyclones
lesson.summary: How weather systems are born — air masses colliding at fronts and the cyclone life cycle.

lesson.title: Thunderstorms and Tornadoes
lesson.summary: The atmosphere's violence — storm structure, how tornadoes form and how we rate them.

lesson.title: Hurricanes and Tropical Cyclones
lesson.summary: Heat engines over warm oceans — cyclone structure, the Saffir-Simpson scale and storm surge.

lesson.title: Observation and Forecasting
lesson.summary: How forecasts are made — observations, satellites, radar and the models behind the seven-day outlook.

lesson.title: Climate Dynamics and Variability
lesson.summary: Beyond weather — ENSO, monsoons, decadal modes and how warming shifts the extremes.

source.qualification: FEPAC Accreditation Standards for forensic science education

forensic-science.note: Units follow FEPAC's required curriculum areas — the scientific foundations, crime-scene investigation, the laboratory disciplines, and the law and ethics that bind them.

units.title: Foundations of forensic science
topics: History and the Locard exchange principle

lesson.title: Foundations of Forensic Science
lesson.summary: What forensic science is — Locard's principle, the lab system and how evidence becomes proof.

lesson.title: Crime Scene Investigation
lesson.summary: The scene is the first laboratory — documentation, search patterns and the chain of custody.

lesson.title: Pattern Evidence: Prints and Bloodstains
lesson.summary: Reading marks left behind — fingerprint examination, bloodstain geometry and impression evidence.

lesson.title: Trace Evidence
lesson.summary: Tiny transfers, big consequences — hairs, fibres, glass, soil and GSR under the comparison microscope.

lesson.title: Forensic Biology and DNA Profiling
lesson.summary: From presumptive tests to STR profiles — the biology that identifies individuals.

lesson.title: Forensic Chemistry and Toxicology
lesson.summary: What's in the blood and the baggie — drug identification, toxicology screens and the instruments behind them.

lesson.title: Ballistics and Digital Forensics
lesson.summary: Bullets and bytes — firearms comparison, digital evidence recovery and questioned documents.

lesson.title: Law, Ethics and the Expert Witness
lesson.summary: Science on trial — admissibility standards, bias and the professional duties of the forensic scientist.

source.qualification: IFT Undergraduate Education Standards for food science degrees
source.document: Published core competencies for food science programmes

food-science.note: Units follow IFT's required competency areas — food chemistry, microbiology, safety, engineering and processing — closing with product development and regulation.

units.title: Food chemistry: the molecules we eat
topics: Carbohydrates, proteins and lipids in food

lesson.title: Food Chemistry Fundamentals
lesson.summary: What food is made of — water activity, the macro molecules and the chemistry of flavour.

lesson.title: Food Microbiology and Fermentation
lesson.summary: The good, the bad and the tasty — spoilage, pathogens and the fermentations we cultivate.

lesson.title: Food Safety and HACCP
lesson.summary: Keeping the supply safe — hazard analysis, critical control points and the modern recall system.

lesson.title: Processing and Preservation
lesson.summary: How food is made shelf-stable — heat, cold, drying and the newer non-thermal methods.

units.title: Food engineering and packaging
topics: Heat and mass transfer in processing

lesson.title: Food Engineering and Packaging
lesson.summary: The engineering behind the meal — unit operations, rheology and the science of the package.

lesson.title: Sensory Science
lesson.summary: Measuring delicious — sensory panels, psychophysics and how preference is quantified.

lesson.title: Product Development
lesson.summary: From bench to shelf — the staged process of building a new food product.

units.title: Food law, regulation and nutrition labelling

lesson.title: Food Law and Labelling
lesson.summary: The rules of the supermarket — labels, additives, GRAS and international standards.

source.qualification: SAF Accreditation Standards for forestry education

forestry.note: Units follow SAF's required curriculum areas — forest biology and ecology, measurement, silviculture and management, and the policy and economics that govern forests.

lesson.title: Forests and Forestry
lesson.summary: What a forest is and what forestry balances — timber, water, wildlife and people.

lesson.title: Forest Ecology and Stand Dynamics
lesson.summary: How forests change — succession, disturbance regimes and the soil engine underneath.

lesson.title: Trees: Biology and Identification
lesson.summary: Knowing the trees — anatomy, growth rings and the species-site relationships silvics codifies.

lesson.title: Forest Mensuration
lesson.summary: Measuring the woods — dbh, basal area, sampling designs and growth-and-yield models.

lesson.title: Silviculture: the Science of Tending Forests
lesson.summary: Growing forests on purpose — regeneration cuts, thinnings and the choice of silvicultural system.

lesson.title: Forest Management and Planning
lesson.summary: Forests as long investments — rotations, management plans and the calculus of sustainable harvest.

lesson.title: Forest Health: Fire, Pests and Disease
lesson.summary: What damages forests and what managers do about it — fire regimes, pests and pathogens.

lesson.title: Forest Policy, Economics and Conservation
lesson.summary: Forests in society — markets, policy, carbon and the conservation of working landscapes.

source.board: Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND)
source.qualification: ACEND Accreditation Standards — coordinated programmes in dietetics

nutrition-dietetics.note: Units follow ACEND's knowledge requirements — the sciences of food and nutrition through the life span, clinical nutrition, and the professional practice of dietetics.

lesson.title: Nutrients and How They Work
lesson.summary: The working vocabulary of nutrition — macros, micros, and what the body does with them.

lesson.title: Digestion, Absorption and Metabolism
lesson.summary: From plate to cell — the digestive pipeline, energy extraction and the body's fuel accounting.

lesson.title: Nutrition Across the Life Span
lesson.summary: Changing needs at every stage — pregnancy, growth, and the nutrition of ageing.

lesson.title: Nutritional Assessment
lesson.summary: Measuring nutritional status — diet records, anthropometry and the labs that flag deficiency.

lesson.title: Nutrition in Chronic Disease
lesson.summary: Food as therapy — the evidence-based nutrition management of diabetes, heart disease and cancer.

lesson.title: Clinical Nutrition in Acute Care
lesson.summary: Feeding the sick patient — screening, enteral and parenteral support and interactions with drugs.

lesson.title: Public Health and Community Nutrition
lesson.summary: Nutrition at population scale — food environments, programmes and the politics of food security.

lesson.title: The Practice of Dietetics
lesson.summary: The profession itself — the nutrition care process, counselling skills and evidence-based standards.
